bypassPaths.path: Do the work without running claim. gh merge, git push, gcloud jobs execute, neon SQL, and any editor on a registered worktree never consult the queue.
bypassPaths.why: Closing this would wrap every write path and turn the queue into a dispatcher. The protocol forbids that. Honestly advisory at those points.

bypassPaths.path: Write claim.json, tokens/store.json, card.json, or a close artifact by hand. This seat did the first two for the lease and token constructs.
bypassPaths.why: The files are the state. A seat that will not ask will not be stopped by prettier files. Advisory, same as not running claim.

bypassPaths.path: Pass --seat property from the integration checkout P:/doc_repo on main. The CLI does not check cwd against the seat worktree.
bypassPaths.why: The operator assigned this chat to seat property. A cwd check would have refused the assigned loop. Seat identity at claim time is a string, not a location.

bypassPaths.path: Pass any --worktree and --branch. claim records them and does not check they exist or are in seat_register.
bypassPaths.why: The dispatch said do not claim a card you cannot name a worktree and branch for. The CLI requires the flags and then believes them. A grant that names a path the seat does not hold is a forged location.

bypassPaths.path: readJson fail-open: a tokens or claim file that exists and does not parse is treated as absent.
bypassPaths.why: This seat's first STORE_TOKEN_HELD construct produced a file and the refusal did not fire. A control that cannot read its own record and reports no token is silent degradation. If the file exists and cannot be parsed, claim should refuse, not proceed as if the store is free.

bypassPaths.path: Edit config.json (empty the window, change weekday) or seat_register.json (move hauska-factory onto another seat).
bypassPaths.why: Those files are the policy. Anyone who can edit them already owns the control. Advisory.

whatContradictedTheCard: The card implied that constructing a held token is enough to fire STORE_TOKEN_HELD. The first construct wrote _queue/tokens/store.json and the CLI refused only MAINTENANCE_WINDOW. readJson returned null, so a present file was no token. A second construct with node-written JSON then fired STORE_TOKEN_HELD. That is the contradiction: the store token is a parsed object, not a file on disk. The decision record is also stale against the tree it describes: it still says 24 assertions and nine refusals; README and self-test.mjs now say 40 cases and ten refusals including NEEDS_OPERATOR_GO. Nothing else on the specified list contradicted the card. factory-merges was CLAIMABLE, the two store cards were refused until 06:00 UTC, and an expired lease became claimable rather than stuck.
